# 8-Bar Mini-Piece: A Minor → C Minor

Here's a sketch that uses your motif, moves through A harmonic minor, pivots through a shared chord, and lands on a strong C minor cadence. Eighth notes throughout in the melody, one or two chords per bar in the left hand.

## Bar-by-Bar

**Bar 1 — A minor (tonic established)**
- Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – D – C
- LH: **Am** (A₂ – C₃ – E₃), whole bar
- The motif in its home key, descent sets up bar 2.

**Bar 2 — A harmonic minor (dominant pull)**
- Melody: B – A – G# – A – B – C – E – G#
- LH: **E major** (E₂ – G#₂ – B₂), whole bar
- The G# is the raised 7th, the V chord strengthens A as tonic.

**Bar 3 — A minor (resolution, motif returns)**
- Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – F – E
- LH: **Am** (A₂ – C₃ – E₃) for beats 1–2, then **F major, 1st inversion** (A₂ – C₃ – F₃) for beats 3–4
- The F chord (VI in A minor) is the pivot setup.

**Bar 4 — Pivot chord (F major = VI in Am, IV in Cm)**
- Melody: F – E – D – C – D – E – F – G
- LH: **F major** (F₂ – A₂ – C₃), whole bar
- F major belongs to both keys. The melody drifts upward to prepare the new tonic.

**Bar 5 — Arrival in C minor (new tonic)**
- Melody: C – Eb – G – Ab – G – Eb – D – C
- LH: **Cm** (C₂ – Eb₂ – G₂), whole bar
- The motif reappears in C minor. Eb and Ab announce the key change clearly.

**Bar 6 — C minor subdominant**
- Melody: Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – Eb – D
- LH: **Fm** (F₂ – Ab₂ – C₃) for beats 1–2, then **Ab major, 1st inversion** (C₃ – Eb₃ – Ab₃) for beats 3–4
- Fm (iv) and Ab (VI) deepen the minor color.

**Bar 7 — C harmonic minor (dominant preparation)**
- Melody: D – Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – D
- LH: **G major** (G₂ – B₂ – D₃), whole bar
- B natural is the raised 7th. G major is V in C harmonic minor, setting up the final cadence.

**Bar 8 — C minor cadence**
- Melody: Eb – D – C – B – C – Eb – G – C
- LH: **G major** (G₂ – B₂ – D₃) for beats 1–2, then **Cm** (C₂ – Eb₂ – G₂) for beats 3–4
- Hold the final C (and the Cm chord) as a half or whole note. This is a V–i perfect authentic cadence.

## Chord Summary

| Bar | Chord(s) | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Am | i in A minor |
| 2 | E major | V in A harmonic minor |
| 3 | Am → F/A | i → VI |
| 4 | F major | Pivot (VI in Am = IV in Cm) |
| 5 | Cm | i in C minor |
| 6 | Fm → Ab/C | iv → VI |
| 7 | G major | V in C harmonic minor |
| 8 | G major → Cm | V → i (authentic cadence) |

## Performance Tips
Play the left-hand chords on the downbeat (and beat 3 where two chords are shown), letting them ring under the eighth-note melody. Take it slowly at first — around 70 BPM — and lean into the G# in bar 2 and the B natural in bar 7, since those accidentals are what make the minor key sound pull toward its tonic. The F major chord in bar 4 is the hinge: linger on it slightly so the ear accepts the move to C minor in bar 5.

Try it through a few times, and if any bar feels awkward under the hand, let me know and we can revoice it.

# 8-Bar Mini-Piece — Piano Reading Sheet

**Tempo:** ♩ = 72 (Andante)
**Dynamics:** mf (bars 1–4) → mp (bars 5–6) → mf with slight crescendo into the final cadence (bars 7–8)

---

**Bar 1 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – D – C
LH: **Am** (A2 – C3 – E3), whole bar

**Bar 2 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: B – A – G# – A – B – C – E – G#
LH: **E major** (E2 – G#2 – B2), whole bar

**Bar 3 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – F – E
LH: **Am** (A2 – C3 – E3) beats 1–2 / **F/A** (A2 – C3 – F3) beats 3–4

**Bar 4 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: F – E – D – C – D – E – F – G
LH: **F major** (F2 – A2 – C3), whole bar *(pivot chord — linger slightly)*

**Bar 5 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: C – Eb – G – Ab – G – Eb – D – C
LH: **Cm** (C2 – Eb2 – G2), whole bar

**Bar 6 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – Eb – D
LH: **Fm** (F2 – Ab2 – C3) beats 1–2 / **Ab/C** (C3 – Eb3 – Ab3) beats 3–4

**Bar 7 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: D – Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – D
LH: **G major** (G2 – B2 – D3), whole bar *(B natural = raised 7th)*

**Bar 8 — 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**
Melody: Eb – D – C – B – C – Eb – G – C
LH: **G major** (G2 – B2 – D3) beats 1–2 / **Cm** (C2 – Eb2 – G2) beats 3–4
*Hold the final C and Cm chord as a whole note or longer for the cadence.*

---

**Quick reminders:**
- Accidentals to watch: **G#** in bar 2, **Eb/Ab** starting bar 5, **B natural** in bars 7–8.
- The pivot is bar 4 (F major belongs to both keys) — ease into bar 5 rather than rushing.
- Let LH chords ring under the eighth-note melody; no need to re-strike unless a new chord is marked.

Have fun with it!

# 8-Bar Mini-Piece — With Fingerings & Pedal

**Tempo:** ♩ = 72 | **Dynamics:** mf → mp (bar 5) → mf cresc. (bars 7–8)
**Fingering key:** 1 = thumb, 5 = pinky | **Pedal:** ⌐ = press, ⌐⌙ = release & re-press, * = release

---

**Bar 1** — ⌐ (press on beat 1)
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – D – C
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2 *(thumb-under after beat 4)*
LH: **Am** A2–C3–E3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 2** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1)
Melody: B – A – G# – A – B – C – E – G#
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 4
LH: **E major** E2–G#2–B2 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 3** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1, and again on beat 3)
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – F – E
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 3 – 2
LH beats 1–2: **Am** A2–C3–E3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1
LH beats 3–4: **F/A** A2–C3–F3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 4** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1)
Melody: F – E – D – C – D – E – F – G
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5
LH: **F major** F2–A2–C3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 5** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1) *mp*
Melody: C – Eb – G – Ab – G – Eb – D – C
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2 *(same shape as bar 1)*
LH: **Cm** C2–Eb2–G2 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 6** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1, and again on beat 3)
Melody: Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – Eb – D
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2
LH beats 1–2: **Fm** F2–Ab2–C3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1
LH beats 3–4: **Ab/C** C3–Eb3–Ab3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 7** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1) *mf cresc.*
Melody: D – Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – D
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 4 – 3 – 1
LH: **G major** G2–B2–D3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

**Bar 8** — ⌐⌙ (change pedal on beat 1, and again on beat 3) — * (release on final note)
Melody: Eb – D – C – B – C – Eb – G – C
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 5 – 1 *(hold final C)*
LH beats 1–2: **G major** G2–B2–D3 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1
LH beats 3–4: **Cm** C2–Eb2–G2 | fingers: 5 – 3 – 1

---

**Pedal rule of thumb:** change pedal on every new chord. If a bar has one chord, one press per bar. If two chords (bars 3, 6, 8), change on beat 3.

**RH fingering tip:** the 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2 pattern in bars 1, 3, and 5 is the motif's "home shape." Once your hand learns it, those bars become muscle memory.

**LH tip:** the 5 – 3 – 1 voicing works for every chord here since they're all three-note triads. Keep the hand position relaxed and let the pedal connect chord changes.

Play it through slowly at first (half tempo is fine), then bring it up to 72 BPM when the fingering feels secure. Enjoy!

# 8-Bar Mini-Piece — Simplified LH (Single Bass Notes)

**Tempo:** ♩ = 72 | **Dynamics:** mf → mp (bar 5) → mf cresc. (bars 7–8)
**Pedal:** ⌐ = press, * = release | **LH:** one bass note per beat, finger shown once (same finger throughout unless noted)

---

**Bar 1** — ⌐ (press on beat 1)
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – D – C
LH: **A2** on each beat (1, 2, 3, 4) | finger: **5**

**Bar 2** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1)
Melody: B – A – G# – A – B – C – E – G#
LH: **E2** on each beat | finger: **5**

**Bar 3** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1, and again on beat 3)
Melody: C – E – G – A – G – E – F – E
LH beats 1–2: **A2** | finger: **5**
LH beats 3–4: **F2** | finger: **5**

**Bar 4** — (no pedal change — F2 continues from bar 3)
Melody: F – E – D – C – D – E – F – G
LH: **F2** on each beat | finger: **5**

**Bar 5** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1) *mp*
Melody: C – Eb – G – Ab – G – Eb – D – C
LH: **C2** on each beat | finger: **5**

**Bar 6** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1, hold through bar — Fm and Ab share no root change needed if simplified, but keep root motion)
Melody: Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – Eb – D
LH beats 1–2: **F2** | finger: **5**
LH beats 3–4: **Ab2** | finger: **5** *(pedal change on beat 3)*

**Bar 7** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1) *mf cresc.*
Melody: D – Eb – F – G – Ab – G – F – D
LH: **G2** on each beat | finger: **5**

**Bar 8** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 3 for the final cadence) — * (release on last note)
Melody: Eb – D – C – B – C – Eb – G – C
LH beats 1–2: **G2** | finger: **5**
LH beats 3–4: **C2** | finger: **5** *(hold final C long)*

---

## Pedal Summary (Minimal)

| Bar | Pedal Action |
|---|---|
| 1 | Press on beat 1 |
| 2 | Change on beat 1 |
| 3 | Change on beats 1 and 3 |
| 4 | No change (F continues) |
| 5 | Change on beat 1 |
| 6 | Change on beats 1 and 3 |
| 7 | Change on beat 1 |
| 8 | Change on beat 3, release after final note |

## Even Simpler Option — One Bass Note Per Bar
If you'd rather play just one bass note per bar and let the pedal sustain it:

- Bar 1: A2 | Bar 2: E2 | Bar 3: A2 (half) → F2 (half) | Bar 4: F2
- Bar 5: C2 | Bar 6: F2 (half) → Ab2 (half) | Bar 7: G2 | Bar 8: G2 (half) → C2 (half)

Play the bass note on beat 1 (and beat 3 where the chord changes mid-bar), let the pedal hold it under the melody, and change pedal when the root changes. This gives a clean, hymn-like accompaniment feel that works well under a singer.

## Tips
Using finger **5** throughout keeps your LH anchored and relaxed — your thumb and inner fingers stay free. If any leap feels awkward (like A2 → E2 in bars 1–2, or Ab2 → G2 across bars 6–7), you can switch to finger **4** or **3** briefly for a smoother motion. Keep the bass notes soft so the melody sings on top, especially in the "singer accompaniment" setting.

# 8-Bar Mini-Piece — Transposed Down a Whole Step (G minor → Bb minor)

**Tempo:** ♩ = 72 | **Dynamics:** mf → mp (bar 5) → mf cresc. (bars 7–8)
**Pedal:** ⌐ = press, * = release | **LH:** single bass note per beat, finger **5**

---

**Bar 1** — ⌐ (press on beat 1)
Melody: Bb – D – F – G – F – D – C – Bb
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2
LH: **G2** on each beat

**Bar 2** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1)
Melody: A – G – F# – G – A – Bb – D – F#
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 4
LH: **D2** on each beat
*(F# = raised 7th of G harmonic minor)*

**Bar 3** — ⌐ (change pedal on beats 1 and 3)
Melody: Bb – D – F – G – F – D – Eb – D
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 3 – 2
LH beats 1–2: **G2** | LH beats 3–4: **Eb2**

**Bar 4** — (no pedal change — Eb continues)
Melody: Eb – D – C – Bb – C – D – Eb – F
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5
LH: **Eb2** on each beat
*(Pivot chord: Eb major = VI in Gm = IV in Bbm)*

**Bar 5** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1) *mp*
Melody: Bb – Db – F – Gb – F – Db – C – Bb
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2
LH: **Bb1** on each beat
*(New key: Bb minor — Db and Gb announce the change)*

**Bar 6** — ⌐ (change pedal on beats 1 and 3)
Melody: Db – Eb – F – Gb – F – Eb – Db – C
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2
LH beats 1–2: **Eb2** | LH beats 3–4: **Gb2**

**Bar 7** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 1) *mf cresc.*
Melody: C – Db – Eb – F – Gb – F – Eb – C
RH fingers: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 4 – 3 – 1
LH: **F2** on each beat
*(A natural = raised 7th of Bb harmonic minor — appears in bar 8)*

**Bar 8** — ⌐ (change pedal on beat 3) — * (release on final note)
Melody: Db – C – Bb – A – Bb – Db – F – Bb
RH fingers: 3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 5 – 1 *(hold final Bb)*
LH beats 1–2: **F2** | LH beats 3–4: **Bb1**

---

## Chord Roots & Pedal Summary

| Bar | Root(s) | Pedal |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | G (i in Gm) | Press beat 1 |
| 2 | D (V in G harmonic minor, F# raised) | Change beat 1 |
| 3 | G → Eb (i → VI) | Change beats 1, 3 |
| 4 | Eb (pivot: VI in Gm = IV in Bbm) | No change |
| 5 | Bb (i in Bbm) | Change beat 1 |
| 6 | Eb → Gb (iv → VI) | Change beats 1, 3 |
| 7 | F (V setup) | Change beat 1 |
| 8 | F → Bb (V → i, A natural raised 7th) | Change beat 3, release end |

## Key Accidentals to Watch
- **F#** in bar 2 (raised 7th of G harmonic minor)
- **Db, Gb** starting bar 5 (new key: Bb minor has 5 flats)
- **A natural** in bar 8 (raised 7th of Bb harmonic minor — creates the leading-tone pull to Bb)

## Tips
Bb minor is a trickier key to read because of the flats, but it actually sits well under the hand on piano — many of the black keys fall naturally where your longer fingers want to be. The "home shape" fingering (1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 3 – 2 – 1 – 2) still works for bars 1, 3, 5, and 6, so the motif stays consistent under your hand across both keys.

For the LH, **G2** and **D2** in bars 1–2 are a comfortable fifth apart. The leap to **Bb1** in bar 5 is the biggest jump — take a moment to find it visually before you play. If Bb1 feels too low on your piano, you can play **Bb2** instead (still finger 5), which keeps things in a friendlier range for singer accompaniment.

Enjoy exploring it in the new key!
